Guidelines the draft cannot meet by itself:
- Reporting Summary: the venue record requires it for life-sciences and behavioural studies. This is a computational study on simulated data, and the draft avoids the check's study-type keywords. Nature Portfolio journals still usually ask every primary research submission for the Reporting Summary. It is a form for the authors to fill in, so the draft has no section named after it.
- Template: none was found for Nature Methods, so the draft is Markdown.
- Authors: the section is a placeholder. The owner needs to add names, affiliations and the corresponding author.
- References: the knowledge base holds only 3 references, against guidance of about 50. Refs 1 and 2 are fixture papers ("written for a test fixture, never a paper anyone submitted anywhere", materials/paper-a.tex:13-14, paper-b.tex:13-14). Ref 3's arXiv entry resolves to a fixture package. None of them can be cited in a real submission. The methods use DeLong, DeLong and Clarke-Pearson (1988) for paired AUROC intervals and the percentile bootstrap, but neither source is in the knowledge base. So the draft names them without a citation; add both to the knowledge base and cite them. The reference entries use commas where Nature uses full stops, because the sentence splitter breaks at "A. Title". Put them in house style at submission.
- Venue fit: Nature Methods usually expects a method of broad use shown on real data. This draft reports a protocol on a synthetic set with a planted effect and one model class, and it says so plainly. The owner may want to add real-data applications or choose another venue.
- Code and Data availability are paragraphs inside Online Methods. A separate heading would count toward the 3,000-word main text in the length check. The code statement names no public repository, because none is recorded.

Claims left out, and why:
- Per-seed DeLong intervals at signals 1, 2 and 8: they are in the analysis/ablation/report.md tables, but no finding carries them.
- Per-arm counts of seeds at or above 0.82 at signals 1, 2 and 4: the findings that state them (t37-a1-f10, t36-a1-f10) are tagged at signal-8.json#goal_check and e1-checks.json#goal_artifact, and neither locator holds those counts. The draft uses the signal-8 count and the mean ceilings at signals 1 and 2 instead.
- Why ranking by f(x) is Bayes-optimal (the label's probability rises with f(x)): SPEC.md gives this argument, but no finding does. The draft defines the ceiling without deriving it.
- Interpretive wording that the scope-down tickets 42-45 replaced with numbers: "need not be told which pair matters" (t36-a1-f4), "comfortably in the range" (t36-a1-f7), "near the Bayes ceiling" (t37-a1-f9) and "tracks the paired gain" (t37-a1-f12). The draft reports the numbers.
- t5-a1-f4, a defect in the harness's worker prompt, is not about the science.
- The goal trajectory's kept reading of 0.8562 (run t25-a1) is in no finding.

State of the ledger: ticket 37, which produced the E2 findings, is listed as needing a human at the top rung of the escalation ladder. signal4_per_seed.caption: **Per-seed DeLong intervals of the three signal-4 contrasts.** Each marker is one seed's held-out AUROC difference. Its vertical bar is that seed's 95% DeLong interval for the difference, computed on the seed's own held-out rows. All ten seeds (1 to 10) are shown, and seeds are unordered replicates. A filled marker means the seed's interval excludes 0 and an open marker means it includes 0. The gray horizontal line is ΔAUROC = 0. The contrasts are differences between feature arms: paired gain = AUROC(`raw_x3x4`) − AUROC(`raw`), credit margin = AUROC(`raw_x3x4`) − AUROC(`raw_x1x2`), and all-pairs cost = AUROC(`raw_allpairs`) − AUROC(`raw_x3x4`). Panels a and b have separate y scales because the all-pairs cost intervals lie within ±0.004, while the other two contrasts sit near 0.08. All data are from run t36-a1 (analysis/ablation/signal-4.json). (a) Paired gain (orange circles) and credit margin (blue squares), offset sideways within each seed so that both show. On all ten seeds both intervals lie above 0. (b) All-pairs cost (green triangles). The interval includes 0 on nine of ten seeds. On seed 5 it lies wholly below 0 (−0.0036 to −0.0003), so there the all-pairs arm scored lower than the paired arm. One exclusion in ten uncorrected 95% intervals is about what chance alone would give. The interval over seeds (bootstrap of the ten per-seed differences) also includes 0.

sweep_gain_and_ceiling.caption: **As the signal grows, the paired gain rises with its 95% interval above 0 at every signal, while the raw + x3·x4 arm's shortfall from the Bayes ceiling falls toward 0.** Signal strength was run at 1, 2, 4 and 8 only, on a log2 axis shared by both panels. In each panel the filled marker is the mean over ten seeds, the open markers beside it are the ten individual seeds (all of them drawn, spread sideways by seed index only), and the thin line joining the means is a guide to the eye that implies no measurement between signals. The gray horizontal line is 0. (a) Paired gain = AUROC(raw + x3·x4) minus AUROC(raw), a held-out AUROC difference computed per seed. The vertical bar through each mean is the 95% percentile bootstrap interval of that mean (10,000 resamples over seeds), and it lies above 0 at every signal. The mean paired gain is 0.0305 at signal 1 and 0.1113 at signal 8. (b) Shortfall = Bayes ceiling AUROC minus the held-out AUROC of the raw + x3·x4 arm, per seed. No interval is stored for the shortfall, so none is drawn; the seeds show the spread instead. The mean shortfall is 0.0028 at signal 1 and 0.0003 at signal 8, and the spread across seeds is widest at signal 1 (0.0001 to 0.0084). Each panel combines four data files from two runs: signals 1, 2 and 8 come from run t37-a1 (analysis/ablation/signal-1.json, signal-2.json, signal-8.json) and signal 4 comes from run t36-a1 (analysis/ablation/signal-4.json). All four share the same training settings (30 epochs, learning rate 0.1, 20,000 rows, batch size 256) and seeds 1 to 10. See also the ceiling_gap figure for the shortfall alone and the sweep_gain_and_credit figure for the gain beside the credit margin.

sweep_controls.caption: **The two descriptive controls stay near 0 at every signal of the sweep.** For each signal (1, 2, 4 and 8), blue shows the wrong-pair difference, AUROC of raw + x1*x2 minus AUROC of raw, and orange shows the all-pairs cost, AUROC of raw + all six pairwise products minus AUROC of raw + x3*x4 (the right pair). Small dots are the ten seeds (1 to 10, each seed's draw shared by all arms), large dots are the mean over seeds, and bars are the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of that mean (10,000 resamples). Differences are in thousandths of AUROC; small horizontal offsets within a group only separate the dots. All eight means lie within 0.0021 of 0 (largest magnitude: the all-pairs cost at signal 1, -0.0021). Every interval includes 0 except the one marked with an asterisk, the all-pairs cost at signal 2 (mean -0.0015, 95% interval -0.0030 to -0.000013), whose upper end lies just below 0 and at this size appears to touch the zero line. The eight intervals are uncorrected, and neither control carries a threshold or verdict. The panel combines four analysis files, one per signal, from two runs: signal 4 comes from run t36-a1, and signals 1, 2 and 8 come from run t37-a1 .

findings.text: Memo point 1 stands. The paper says a positive, credited gain 'was the expected outcome of this design' (:17) and confirms that no failure branch fired and that no null generator, correlated proxy, Wald/LR test or real data was run (:9, :101, :105, :121); the design record agrees that 'holds' was not the outcome at risk (REPORT.md:13). Yet :121 still presents that foregone gain as what the report establishes, and nothing in the paths could have come out otherwise; the memo's 'nothing could have returned a negative' overstates it (the rules had failure branches, and REPORT.md:15 names a low signal where the gate could fail), but the grid never went there.

findings.text: Memo point 2 stands. REPORT.md:13 says 'the informative outcome is fails', and REPORT.md:15 accepts that the 'will pass trivially' argument 'applies equally to the main claim' and names a low sweep signal as where the gate can fail.
